summary: The bad() method compared `random.getClass()` (always `Random.class`) against `secureRandom.getClass()` (always `SecureRandom.class`). Since these runtime classes can never be equal, `!equals(...)` was a tautology that always evaluated to true (CWE-571). The repair preserves the feature of comparing two objects' runtime classes and printing when they differ, but makes the second object's runtime type depend on a runtime value so the comparison is genuinely data-dependent rather than always true.
